messages:
Anya: Quick sync question — we still don't have a clear call on opaque backing vs split-mapped host pages for GPU offload. RFC left three followups (fragmentation telemetry, compaction cost, tenant fairness). Can we decide or at least agree on a short experiment plan?
Sam: My read: RFC favored opaque backing for correctness and simpler VM semantics, but the fragmentation delta wasn't quantified for small allocations. Folks flagged latency regressions.
Marta: Confirmed — on Dedicated canary we saw an 8-12% P50 regression for small-batch textgen when opaque host-backed pages were enabled across the board. Memory compaction runs more often and stalls small batches.
Li: Quick data dump from the probe run (last week):
```
fragmentation_score: 0.26 -> 0.48 (opaque)
small_alloc_failures: 32 -> 87 per hour
compaction_time_p95: 42ms -> 112ms
```
(opaque vs splitmap baseline). Telemetry collected from tenant A/B.
Anya: Important: we need to balance safety (no alias bugs) vs SLA impact. Options on the table: 1) keep opaque but invest in background coalescer + per-tenant small-page pools, 2) hybrid: split-map only for sizes < X, 3) tenant-scoped policy (legacy customers get splitmap), 4) revert to splitmap and harden alias checks. Thoughts?
Sam: Hybrid seems pragmatic: default opaque, runtime opt-in splitmap for tight-latency tenants. Implementation surface: runtime flag + allocator switching path. Risk: adding two codepaths increases maintenance.
Marta: Hybrid works but we need a cheap heuristic to avoid frequent mode-switching and cross-tenant fragmentation transfer. Suggest: per-tenant small-page reserve + eviction token so small allocations preferentially use a splitmapped pool. That keeps opaque for big objects.
Li: Implementation notes: splitmap requires maintaining aliasing invariants and more complex fault handling. Opaque simplifies DMA/GPUDirect and reduces TLB pressure in our tests. If we do hybrid, ensure the small-pool uses page-size alignment and coalescing background thread.
Anya: Can we add the following telemetry before deciding?
- fragmentation_by_size_bucket (0-64B, 65-1k, 1k-64k, >64k)
- compaction_cost_ms_per_mb
- small_pool_utilization_per_tenant
- allocation_fallback_rate (opaque -> host-staging)
Sam: +1. Also add a perf suite: 1) small-batch gen (batch=1..4), 2) mixed workloads with retries, 3) long-lived embedding jobs. Run on canary and dedicated replica.
Marta: One more real-world concern: compaction can inflate p99 latencies during tenant spikes. If we keep opaque we must be able to throttle compaction aggressively under SLA pressure. Suggest cap compaction work per-second and favor latency-sensitive paths.
Li: Low-level snippet for the coalescer prototype we've been iterating on:
```
while (true) {
  scan_free_runs();
  pick_candidate_runs(max_bytes=8MB);
  attempt_coalesce(candidate);
  if (coalesced) submit_compaction_work();
  sleep(coalesce_interval_ms);
}
```
We can tune max_bytes and interval per-tenant.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of "opaque-offload" feature-flag to cluster "canary-3" completed at 2026-03-18T12:08:00Z :white_check_mark:
Sam: Next step proposal: roll telemetry + perf suites this week, then a 48h splitmap A/B with hybrid candidate next week. If hybrid shows <2% P50 regression and fragmentation drops >15%, consider defaulting hybrid on new clusters.
Anya: Action items:
- Li: add fragmentation_by_size_bucket + compaction_cost metrics (due EOW)
- Marta: run perf suite on canary and post results (due in 3 days)
- Sam: prototype runtime flag + small-page pool sketch (PR smoke, due 1 week)
- Infra: keep canary flagged for another 72h and capture traces
We'll revisit at arch sync Thu. :calendar:
Marta: Also adding doc note on security implications for splitmap (alias windows) — will paste in the thread when done.
Anya: Thanks — this is actionable. If anyone wants to pair on the coalescer knobs ping me.
